messages:
OpsBot: INCIDENT ALERT: autoscale-throttle-surge triggered in prod/us-west-2. throttle_events rate > 120/min across gen-worker pools. Affected services: generation-api, chat-router. Pager opened PD-4521. Severity: P1. Start: 2026-03-15T02:05:09Z.

Maria (oncall): I'm on it. Looking at the gen-worker dashboard — queue depth spiked and tokens/sec per node jumped. Any direct customer reports yet?

PagerDuty Bot: PD-4521 assigned to Maria (oncall) and Kevin.

Maria (oncall): I'll take mitigation. Initial plan: reduce batch size and enable fallback queued-mode for non-urgent requests. Rolling a hotfix to a subset of workers now.

Kevin: Heads-up — lowering batch size will raise per-token cost and could increase latency. Suggest we also route embed/bulk jobs to the best-effort pool while we stabilize. I can open a routing tweak.

Sam: Observability FYI — hosted customers seeing error rate climb: baseline 0.2% -> 1.8% over the last 10m. Not huge but noticeable.

Nadia: Customer impact summary ping: some low-latency SLAs (<=50ms) timed out. Support alerted for affected accounts.

Maria (oncall): Applying runtime patch now: set BATCH_MAX down from 128 to 32 for gen-workers. Command I used:

```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/gen-workers BATCH_MAX=32
kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/gen-workers --watch
```

OpsBot: DEPLOYMENT_EVENT: rollout started by Maria (oncall). image=gen-worker:v1.4.3-hotfix. 30% pods updated.

Ankit: We're also seeing autoscaler flapping — scale-up/scale-down cycles causing capacity churn. We should debounce the queue_depth alert and add a short for: window to avoid noise. Current prom rule (simplified):

```
ALERT HighQueueDepth
  IF avg_over_time(queue_depth[1m]) > 500
  LABELS { severity="page" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="High queue depth" }
```

Ankit: Proposed emergency change: raise threshold and require sustained signal:

```
ALERT HighQueueDepth
  IF avg_over_time(queue_depth[3m]) > 1000
  FOR 3m
  LABELS { severity="page" }
```

Ankit: Also add a separate alert for throttle events so we don't conflate short bursts with sustained saturation:

```
ALERT ThrottleEventSpike
  IF increase(throttle_events_total[2m]) > 50
  FOR 2m
  LABELS { severity="warning" }
```

Kevin: Agreed. I'll open an emergency PR to alerts repo with those changes and request a 15m review. Also creating a quick routing change to move non-critical traffic to best-effort pool: `/routing set priority=low -> pool=best-effort` (will test on 10% first).

Maria (oncall): Customer impact note added to PD-4521: ~1.2% of requests affected across multiple tenants; peak error window ~02:06-02:14 UTC. CS ticket created: CS-789. Support notified.

Sam: After the batch-size tweak latency improved ~20% on the updated pods. Throttle events dropped: 18/min on updated nodes vs 120/min pre-change.

OpsBot: ALERT_UPDATED: autoscale-throttle-surge cleared automatically at 2026-03-15T02:12:45Z. Some alerts still firing as warnings. PD-4521 remains open for follow-up.

Maria (oncall): Post-incident action items (quick list):
- Tune queue_depth alert threshold and add `for` window (Ankit).
- Add tokens/sec per-node panel to the default SLO dashboard and create a short playbook snippet explaining normal ranges (Sam).
- Implement routing policy for low-priority/bulk jobs during saturation and test 10% rollout (Kevin).
- Customer impact writeup and notification summary (Nadia).
- Create postmortem and link to PD-4521; target publish in 48h (Maria).

Kevin: :thumbsup: opening PR now -> alerts/infra#emergency/PD-4521. Will request expedited review from Ankit.

Ankit: After PR merge we'll run a canary for alert change in staging for 30m, then prod. Also adding a temporary dashboard panel: `throttle_events_rate` over host.

Maria (oncall): I'm going to monitor for 35m then hand off long-term monitoring to Kevin. If anything spikes again, page me immediately.

OpsBot: HANDOFF: PD-4521 handoff scheduled Maria -> Kevin in 35m. Reminder set.

Maria (oncall): Thanks team — good mitigation. We'll follow up with a full postmortem and concrete threshold numbers once we validate the new thresholds against historical traffic.

Kevin: Will also add a short entry in the runbook under "capacity saturation" for routing fallback and batch-size rollback steps.

Sam: I'll keep the dashboard and logs open and post a short update in PD-4521 once PR merged and alerts updated.

Nadia: Noting action item to coordinate with CS for impacted customers; will draft a summary and include suggested compensations if required.

OpsBot: NOTE: automated snapshot of dashboards and logs attached to PD-4521.

Maria (oncall): Closing live mitigation thread here — moving to follow-up ticket. If anything else arises, reopen thread or page.
